skills.name: tooling-power-bi
skills.description: The Power BI Agent designs and reviews Power BI datasets and reports: the data model, DAX measures, refresh and lineage, row-level security, and performance. Use when a Power BI dataset or report needs a data-model or DAX review, or refresh, incremental refresh, or data lineage needs designing.

skills.name: tooling-qlik
skills.description: The Qlik Dashboard Agent brings the SDK's engineering discipline to Qlik. Use when a dashboard spec needs to be delivered in Qlik, or a Qlik dashboard needs a review for honest charts, governance, or the associative data model, set analysis, and section-access security.

skills.name: tooling-react
skills.description: The React Dashboard Agent brings the SDK's engineering discipline to web dashboards built in React. Use when a dashboard spec needs to be rendered as a React application, or a React dashboard needs a review for accessible, non-misleading charts.

skills.name: tooling-streamlit-dash
skills.description: The Streamlit Dashboard Agent brings engineering discipline to Python-native dashboards built in Streamlit. Use when a dashboard spec needs to be delivered as a Streamlit app, or a Streamlit app needs a review for caching, reruns, honest charts, or secrets.

skills.name: tooling-superset
skills.description: The Superset Dashboard Agent brings the SDK's engineering discipline to Superset. Use when a dashboard spec needs to be delivered in Superset, or a Superset dashboard needs a review for honest charts, governance, or SQL/dataset governance, Jinja templating safety, and caching.

skills.name: tooling-tableau
skills.description: The Tableau Agent designs and reviews Tableau workbooks and data sources: extract-vs-live choices, calculations (LOD and table calcs), honest visualization, performance, and publishing/permissions. Use when a Tableau workbook or data source needs a correctness or performance review, or level-of-detail (LOD) or table calculations are producing wrong or confusing results.

skills.name: trading-strategies-carry
skills.description: The Carry Agent designs and reviews carry and roll-down strategies across asset classes: FX carry, fixed-income carry and roll-down, commodity carry (backwardation/contango), and dividend/equity carry. Use when a carry or roll-down strategy needs designing or reviewing, or the carry-to-risk trade-off and tail behavior need assessment.

skills.name: trading-strategies-event-driven-arbitrage
skills.description: The Event-Driven & Arbitrage Agent designs and reviews event-driven strategies: merger/risk arbitrage, index rebalancing, earnings and corporate-action events, convertible arbitrage, and special situations. Use when a merger-arb, index-rebalance, earnings, or convertible-arb strategy is proposed, or event definitions and their point-in-time dating need scrutiny.

skills.name: trading-strategies-macro-multi-asset
skills.description: The Macro & Multi-Asset Agent designs and reviews macro and allocation strategies: global macro, tactical and strategic asset allocation, risk parity, and cross-asset tilts. Use when a global-macro, allocation, or risk-parity strategy needs designing or reviewing, or macro signals built on revised economic data need a point-in-time check.

skills.name: trading-strategies-market-making-microstructure
skills.description: The Market Making & Microstructure Agent designs and reviews liquidity-provision and microstructure strategies: market making, execution alpha, and order-book/short-horizon strategies. Use when a market-making, execution, or order-book strategy needs designing or reviewing, or adverse selection and inventory risk need assessment.

skills.name: trading-strategies-mean-reversion-statarb
skills.description: The Mean Reversion & Statistical Arbitrage Agent designs and reviews mean-reversion strategies: pairs trading, cointegration-based stat arb, and index/ETF arbitrage. Use when a pairs, cointegration, or stat-arb strategy needs designing or reviewing, or a mean-reverting relationship needs a stability and half-life assessment.

skills.name: trading-strategies-momentum-trend
skills.description: The Momentum & Trend Agent designs and reviews momentum and trend-following strategies: cross-sectional momentum (rank winners vs losers), time-series momentum, and trend-following (CTA-style). Use when a momentum or trend signal needs designing or reviewing, or lookback, holding period, and skip-month choices need justification.

skills.name: trading-strategies-value-factor
skills.description: The Value & Factor Agent designs and reviews factor strategies: value, quality, size, low-volatility, profitability, and other cross-sectional style factors. Use when a value or factor strategy needs designing or reviewing, or factor definitions and their point-in-time construction need scrutiny.

skills.name: trading-strategies-volatility-options
skills.description: The Volatility & Options Agent designs and reviews volatility and options strategies: variance risk premium harvesting, volatility arbitrage (implied vs realized), dispersion, options overlays, and VIX/variance strategies. Use when a volatility or options strategy needs designing or reviewing, or implied-vs-realized or dispersion trades need assessment.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-collection-gap-tracker
skills.description: The Collection Gap Tracker Agent turns evidence gaps into a register of information requirements — what question, why it matters to a decision, what lawful public or licensed sources could answer it, and its status — for the accountable human to approve. Use when an analytic product has open gaps that limit its conclusion, or a team needs to prioritise which missing evidence matters most to a stated decision.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-company-diligence
skills.description: The Company Diligence Agent assembles a structured diligence memo from evidence the caller supplies about one company: documents, filings, signals, and structure maps. Use when a candidate company needs a structured diligence memo from supplied evidence, or claims in a pitch deck or data room must be checked against independent evidence.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-competing-hypotheses-analyst
skills.description: The Competing Hypotheses Analyst Agent builds a transparent matrix of competing hypotheses against the evidence — including a deception or measurement-artifact hypothesis — to show which evidence discriminates between them and how sensitive the result is. Use when a thesis rests on signals that more than one explanation could produce, or a surprising signal may be a deception, a data artifact (backfill, survivorship), or a real change.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-confidence-language-reviewer
skills.description: The Confidence Language Reviewer Agent reviews the wording of analytic judgements for calibrated likelihood language tied to the standard probability bands, keeps likelihood separate from confidence in the evidence, and flags vague or unsupported wording. Use when a draft memo, brief, or landscape contains judgements that need consistent likelihood wording, or a judgement states a probability and its word may not match the band.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-deal-sourcing
skills.description: The Deal Sourcing Agent discovers candidate companies from the signal channels and screens them against criteria the caller states, producing a longlist with the evidence and coverage behind each entry. Use when a thesis or technology area needs a longlist of candidate companies, or candidates must be screened against explicit criteria (stage, region, domain, signal thresholds).

skills.name: venture-intelligence-dual-use-indicator
skills.description: The Dual-Use Indicator Agent flags indicators that a technology, product, or research area may be dual-use or subject to export or technology controls, by matching descriptions against control lists the caller supplies, and turns each into a question for counsel. Use when a technology landscape or company profile touches areas that may be controlled (for example advanced computing, semiconductors, quantum, biotechnology, aerospace, advanced materials), or product or patent descriptions need comparing with a caller-supplied control list.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-entity-resolution
skills.description: The Entity Resolution Agent compares company records from different sources, scripts, and jurisdictions and reports whether they are the same legal entity, using registry identifiers and LEIs first and names only as candidates — never merging on a name alone. Use when records from two sources may describe the same company and a cross-source join is needed, or names appear in different scripts or transliterations (e.g. Hanzi and pinyin, Thai and Latin).

skills.name: venture-intelligence-fund-performance-analyst
skills.description: The Fund Performance Analyst Agent computes and explains venture fund performance from dated cash flows: DPI, RVPI, and TVPI as of a date, XIRR with its roots and warnings, the J-curve cash profile and its report-date series, Kaplan-Schoar PME against a supplied index, and the percentile rank among vintage-matched peers the caller supplies. Use when a fund's performance needs reporting at a date, using only what was known then, or early-life metrics need explaining against the J-curve rather than compared with mature funds.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-hiring-signal-analyst
skills.description: The Hiring Signal Analyst Agent reads hiring and workforce signals at the organization level — posting volumes, role mix, skill demand, and geography by company or sector — as a lead indicator of growth, pivots, or contraction, without profiling any individual. Use when a company or sector's growth or contraction needs a lead indicator, or role and skill mix is wanted to infer a technology direction (e.g. a shift toward machine-learning or hardware roles).

skills.name: venture-intelligence-intelligence-brief-writer
skills.description: The Intelligence Brief Writer Agent drafts a bottom-line-up-front intelligence brief from cited, graded passages retrieved under the caller's clearance: a short BLUF, then evidence, assumptions, judgements, and open gaps kept in separate sections, with calibrated likelihood wording and an evidence-confidence level on every judgement. Use when a technology landscape, signal thesis, or screening-support result needs a written brief for a reader, or findings from several agents must be assembled into one product without losing their citations or grades.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-investment-memo-writer
skills.description: The Investment Memo Writer Agent drafts an investment memo for the investment committee from approved diligence, tradecraft, and fund outputs and cited passages: evidence, assumptions, judgements, and open gaps in separate sections, with the decision owner named. Use when a candidate company or fund has diligence, signal, and performance work that needs assembling into a committee memo, or a memo must show what is established, what is assumed, and what is still unknown.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-multilingual-document-nlp
skills.description: The Multilingual Document NLP Agent extracts structured, source-anchored facts from start-up financial and legal documents written in Mandarin (Simplified and Traditional), Japanese, Korean, Bahasa Indonesia/Malay, Vietnamese, Thai, Filipino, and English (including South Asian business English with lakh and crore), and normalizes them so figures and parties are comparable across languages and jurisdictions. Use when a term sheet, shareholder agreement, financial statement, prospectus/offering document, registry filing, or pitch deck is not in English or is bilingual, or figures, dates, or party names must be made comparable across documents in different languages or accounting conventions.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-narrative-news-analyst
skills.description: The Narrative and News Analyst Agent turns multilingual news and narrative data into signals about companies, technologies, and sectors — separating original reporting from syndication and promotion, and events from sentiment — while keeping provenance and source grade attached to every item. Use when a company, technology, or sector needs a news-based signal or timeline, or coverage is in several languages (e.g. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Bahasa, Vietnamese, Thai) and must be compared on one footing.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-ownership-screen
skills.description: The Ownership Screen Agent assembles ownership and foreign-capital indicators for a company from structure maps, registry facts, and restricted-party list matches, computes effective ownership through chains, and reports indicators with confidence and unresolved layers. Use when structure maps from the regional structure analysts need consolidating into an ownership and capital-source view, or effective ownership through multi-layer chains must be computed against caller-supplied thresholds.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-patent-ip-analyst
skills.description: The Patent and IP Analyst Agent turns patent and intellectual-property records into landscape signals for technology scouting: filing and publication trends by technology domain and assignee, patent families rather than raw filings, and cross-office coverage including the Chinese, Japanese, Korean, European, US, and international (WIPO) offices. Use when a technology domain, company, or competitor set needs a patent landscape, or filings from several offices and languages (e.g. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, English) must be compared on one footing.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-portfolio-reserve-analyst
skills.description: The Portfolio Reserve Analyst Agent runs seeded simulations of venture fund outcomes and follow-on reserve policy — heavy-tailed company outcomes, a bootstrap from a supplied cohort, an equal-outcome null, tail sensitivity, and a reserve-fraction table — and reports distributions with intervals and every assumption. Use when a fund's outcome distribution needs framing under a heavy-tailed assumption, or alternative reserve fractions need comparing on identical simulated outcomes.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-source-reliability-grader
skills.description: The Source Reliability Grader Agent proposes a source-reliability grade (A to F) and an information-credibility grade (1 to 6), graded separately, for each source and item in an analytic product, with the basis for each grade stated. Use when an analytic product, longlist, or memo needs its sources and items graded, or a new source or vendor panel must be graded before its signals are used.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-technology-landscape-analyst
skills.description: The Technology Landscape Analyst Agent maps a technology domain across patents, publications, open-source activity, grants and procurement, and hiring signals into a landscape: who works on what, where, and how fast the activity is growing, with the coverage and bias of each channel stated and readiness reported only as sources state it. Use when a technology domain (e.g. a battery chemistry, a class of AI model, a semiconductor process) needs a landscape for scouting, or signals from several channels must be combined, with corroboration across independent channels.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-valuation-marks-reviewer
skills.description: The Valuation Marks Reviewer Agent reviews private-company valuation marks for internal consistency and returns flags with the numbers behind them — a missing basis, a stale mark, a mark-up with no new round, a mark that predates the latest round, a down round not reflected, or a price far from the last round. Use when a set of quarter-end marks needs a consistency review before it goes to the valuation committee, or a new priced round has appeared and the existing marks must be checked against it.

skills.name: venture-intelligence-venture-orchestrator
skills.description: The Venture Orchestrator Agent routes a plain-language venture or non-traditional-intelligence request to the right chain of agents, with the review gates, decision owner, decision-path class, and clearance the work needs, or refuses the parts of a request the suite must never perform and names the human who owns that decision. Use when a request touches technology scouting, portfolio consulting, or foreign-influence screening support and it is unclear which agents to use, or a request names one or more Asian markets and the regional leads and structure analysts must be chosen.

skills.name: workflow-orchestrator
skills.description: The Workflow Orchestrator Agent drives a change through the full spec-driven lifecycle. Use when a new request needs to be taken from idea to shipped, not just one stage done, or you want the spec-driven gates enforced across the whole lifecycle.
